title: Fix Puzzle 2D Performance Regression Round 4: Live Cross-Pane Gesture Sync
description: Puzzle 2D board used to be very performant at the `premigration` git tag; after the migration from the bespoke `puzzle/2d/react/index.tsx` renderer to the generic framework shell + Rust/WASM BoardHost pipeline, zoom and selection now take multiple seconds. Root-cause refactor per plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/puzzle-2d-used-to-piped-balloon.md: (1) restore rAF-coalesced rendering in framework/renderer/react/components/puzzle-2d-board-host.tsx (no more synchronous renderFrame()/dispatch per raw pointer/wheel event), (2) stop hover setters from bumping content_scene_generation in mathematical/graph/port/directed/normal/rs/lib.rs, (3) stop puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs from re-stringifying the whole fixture 3x per action, (4) parallelize framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx refreshUi()'s sequential awaits, (5) add spatial partitioning to hit-testing in the graph engine.
summary:
Fixed a flicker the user reported right after Round 4 shipped: "whenever something is finalized it shortly flickers back to the last state before updating correctly" (e.g. after a drag).

Root cause: `applyPendingFixtureIfReady`/`applyPendingSelectionIfReady` (in `framework/renderer/react/components/puzzle-2d-board-host.tsx`) stash a scene/selection update that arrives while deferred (own drag, camera interaction, or — as of Round 4 — a peer owning the live gesture) into `pendingFixtureSceneRef`/`pendingSelectionJsonRef`, then apply it once the deferring condition clears. The bug: on every gesture end (pointerUp/pointerLeave/Escape-cancel), this pending value was applied unconditionally — but it's typically STALE, captured from an early mid-gesture flush (a node-drag's `pointerDownScreen` always pushes a `select` event, which is in `PUZZLE2D_FLUSH_NOW_EVENT_NAMES` and triggers an immediate plugin round-trip partway through the drag, well before the final position is known). Applying that stale snapshot right as the gesture ends, followed moments later by the *actual* fresh commit's response, produced the flicker: correct live state -> stale pre-commit snapshot -> correct committed state.

Fix: added `settleGestureEnd(session)` in the same file — it drains events first (so it knows whether a flush is about to go out), and only applies the pending fixture/selection when nothing is pending to flush; when a flush *is* imminent, it discards the stale pending value instead of applying it, since the flush response will supersede it a moment later anyway. Wired this into `onPointerUp`, `onPointerLeave`, and the Escape area-select-cancel path (replacing the old `applyPendingFixtureIfReady` + `flushBoardEvents()` pairing with `settleGestureEnd` + `dispatchBufferedEvents()`). Extended `notifyPuzzle2dPeersGestureEnded`/`Puzzle2dBoardPeer.onPeerGestureEnded` with a `flushed: boolean` parameter so sibling panes apply the same discard-vs-apply decision instead of always eagerly re-applying their own stale pending echo.

Updated one existing test (`notifies peers when a gesture ends...`) to cover the new `flushed` parameter. Full suite: 147/147 passing. Verified live at :6012 (Concrete Forest example): a real drag still mirrors live across all three panes and settles cleanly with no visible regression; frame-level flicker timing itself could not be captured via automated screenshots (the browser-automation pane throttles rAF/timers and clears the WebGPU canvas's drawing buffer between frames when backgrounded, making sub-16ms flicker capture infeasible with available tooling) — the fix is verified by code-level root-cause tracing (confirmed against the exact Rust engine event-flush logic) plus full regression testing, not by an automated before/after flicker screenshot. Recommend the user do a quick visual confirmation in their own live session.
